text: Imagine putting a fork in the microwave and pressing start.
Most people think the metal makes it explode.
But the inside of your microwave is already made of metal.
The walls bounce the waves around like mirrors until they soak into the water in your food.
The problem with a fork is its shape.
The waves shove tiny charges back and forth inside the metal and they pile up at the sharp tips.
When enough pile up the air around the tips breaks down and the charge jumps through it as a spark.
That's a tiny bolt of lightning right next to your dinner.
And if there's paper nearby like a takeout box those sparks can start a fire.
But a smooth spoon has no sharp tips so it usually barely sparks at all.
So it's not the metal that's dangerous it's the points.
Share this with someone who microwaves everything and subscribe for more.
